newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU vets BAe/Rheinmetall control of STN Atlas.
newsitem.headline: EU vets BAe/Rheinmetall control of STN Atlas.

text.p: The European Commission said on Friday it was starting a routine probe into the joint control of military equipment firm STN Atlas Elektronik GmbH by British Aerospace Plc (BAe) and German defence and engineering group Rheinmetall AG.
STN Atlas was sold in November for 550 million marks by the official receiver of its parent, bankrupt German shipyard group Bremer Vulkan.

The Commission said in a statement the deal was submitted for clearance on March 7 under the EU's merger regulation which bans creation or strengthening of dominant positions. It has a month to clear the operation or start a full probe which could last another four months.

The Commission did not provide any details on the deal. But according to press reports Rheinmetall would own 26 percent of STN Atlas while taking management control. German utility Badenwerk would have another 25 percent and BAe 49 percent.
The Commission called on third parties to comment within 10 days of publication of the statement in the EU's Official Journal, which must happen shortly.
